set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 1a Step 1.

Friends is a clean test corpus: the mapper has never been run on it. The pool is 23 participants and 630 WhichEvent gold units (veridical recall only). Aggregate recall-order statistics (74.1% non-decreasing) were already computed over all 23, so the split is model-untouched, not unseen.

Scope:
Draw, commit and guard the split before any model output on Friends exists.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A committed script draws a participant-level split with a committed seed; membership, seed, script hash and per-side counts (participants, gold units) are committed before any model output on Friends exists.
2. Power assumptions and the minimum detectable effect for the primary estimand (participant-average accuracy difference) are recorded at draw time, method stated.
3. The exposure statement above is committed with the split.
4. A guard module refuses test participants unless called in an explicit final-opening mode that requires the release-candidate manifest hash. The commit lists every code path that reads Friends recall (by file) and each imports the guard; a test greps tools/ and the Scala sources for readers of the Friends recall path and fails if any reader bypasses the guard; a mutation removing the guard fails the refusal test.
5. A read-count ledger for the Friends test split is committed and records zero reads.

Gate: every script in tools/recall-study/tests exits 0 (`for t in tools/recall-study/tests/test_*.py;
do python3 "$t" || exit 1; done`), new tests included; a named mutation witness per new guard; no
recall prose or participant text committed (hashes and aggregates only); fresh-context cold review;
the commit body states the evidence and what it does not establish.

Size: S.
set.title: Phase 1a: draw and seal the Friends participant-level test split
